Main.sentence: Maya Kasandra Soetoro-Ng ( née Soetoro ; /ˈmaɪ.ə suːˈtɔːroʊ ˈɪŋ/ ;  born August 15, 1970) is an Indonesian-born American academic, who is a faculty specialist at the ___E:Spark M. Matsunaga Institute for Peace and Conflict Resolution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spark_M._Matsunaga_Institute_for_Peace_and_Conflict_Resolution)___ , based in the College of Social Sciences at the ___E:University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Hawai%CA%BBi_at_M%C4%81noa)___ .
She is also a consultant for the Obama Foundation, working to develop the Asia-Pacific Leaders Program.
Soetoro-Ng is the maternal half-sister of ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ , the 44th president of the United States.

Soetoro-Ng was born in Saint Carolus Hospital, a Catholic hospital, in ___E:Jakarta U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jakarta)___ , Indonesia,  the daughter of American ___E:cultural anthropologist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_anthropologist)___ ___E:Ann Dunham U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ann_Dunham)___ (1942–1995), an American of Swiss, German, Irish, Scottish, Welsh and English descent and ___E:Indonesian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indonesians)___ businessman ___E:Lolo Soetoro U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lolo_Soetoro)___ (1935–1987).

She had two half-brothers, ___E:Barack Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama)___ (born 1961), the 44th president of the United States, and Bayu Yusuf Aji Soetoro (born 1981), and a half-sister, Rahayu Nurmaida Soetoro (born 1984).
She also had an adoptive sister, Holiah Soetoro (1957–2010).
Soetoro-Ng has said she was ___E:named after U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namesake)___ American poet ___E:Maya Angelou U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maya_Angelou)___ .

Soetoro-Ng and Obama spent several years together in Indonesia and in ___E:Hawaii U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hawaii)___ before her mother decided to return to Indonesia with her.  After her parents divorced in 1980, her father remarried.
From this marriage, Soetoro-Ng has another half-brother and a half-sister, who are of no relation or familial connection to Obama.
While living in Indonesia, Soetoro-Ng was home-schooled by her mother.
From 1981 to 1984, Soetoro-Ng attended ___E:Jakarta International School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jakarta_International_School)___ .

Like Obama, Soetoro-Ng returned to Hawaii and attended the private ___E:Punahou School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punahou_School)___ in ___E:Honolulu U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honolulu)___ , Hawaii,  graduating in 1988.
Soetoro-Ng received her B.A. degree from ___E:Barnard College of Columbia University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barnard_College_of_Columbia_University)___ .

She then received an ___E:M.A. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Arts)___ in secondary language studies and an ___E:M.A. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Arts)___ in Secondary Education from ___E:New York University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_University)___ .

In 2006, she received a ___E:Ph.D. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doctor_of_Philosophy)___ in international comparative education from the ___E:University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Hawai%CA%BBi_at_M%C4%81noa)___ .
According to The New York Times , Soetoro-Ng "has often spoken warmly about her relationship with her older brother" and their families have "often celebrated Christmas in Hawaii" together.

Soetoro-Ng is currently a faculty specialist for the ___E:Spark M. Matsunaga Institute for Peace and Conflict Resolution U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spark_M._Matsunaga_Institute_for_Peace_and_Conflict_Resolution)___ , which is based in the College of Social Sciences at the ___E:University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Hawai%CA%BBi_at_M%C4%81noa)___ , as well as a consultant for the Obama Foundation's Leaders Program: Asia-Pacific.
Dr. Soetoro-Ng teaches courses on: Peace Education; the History of Peace Movements; and Leadership for Social Change.

She also oversees ___E:externships U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Externship)___ for undergraduates who are majoring or minoring in Peace Studies and coordinates the institute's community and global ___E:service learning programs U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Service_learning_programs)___ .

Soetoro-Ng was an assistant professor at the Institute for Teacher Education at the University of Hawai'i College of Education and continues to do some consulting work, promoting international exchange and understanding, in partnership with the East West Center.

She authored a children's book, Ladder to the Moon , that was inspired by her mother and her daughter, Suhaila; it was published in 2011.   She is working on a book about peace education and a young adult novel entitled Yellowood.

Soetoro-Ng was a high school history teacher at ___E:La Pietra: Hawaii School for Girls U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/La_Pietra:_Hawaii_School_for_Girls)___ and the ___E:Education Laboratory School U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Education_Laboratory_School)___ , both in ___E:Honolulu, Hawaii U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Honolulu)___ .

She previously taught and developed curriculum at The Learning Project, an alternative public ___E:middle school U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_school)___ in ___E:New York City U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_City)___ , from 1996 to 2000.
In 2009, Soetoro-Ng helped bring her mother's dissertation to publication in the form of the book Surviving against the Odds: Village Industry in Indonesia .
She wrote a foreword to the book and participated in its launch at the American Anthropological Association annual meeting.

In 2019, Soetoro-Ng, along with Todd Shuster and Jennifer Gates cofounded The Peace Studio: a non-profit organization whose mission is to support, train and unite the next generation of artists, journalists and storytellers to inspire people everywhere to become active peacebuilders.
Soetoro-Ng's doctoral research at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa focused on Multicultural and International Education.
She examined the use of narrative to develop more complex understandings of identity in multicultural classrooms.
She promoted the learning of Social Studies—history and current events—from multiple perspectives.
She has developed and implemented peace education curricula in public high schools and for K-12 teachers in Colleges of Education.

With partner Kerrie Urosevich, she founded the nonprofit Ceeds of Peace (ceedsofpeace.org), which connects families, community leaders and educators in a 360 degree approach to raise and educate peacebuilding leaders.

With environmental law professor Maxine Burkett, she co-founded the nonprofit, Institute for Climate and Peace (www.climateandpeace.org) which works for ___E:climate justice U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Climate_justice)___ at the intersection of climate change and positive peacebuilding.

In May 2007, Soetoro-Ng announced that she would assist Obama in his campaign for presidency,   and took two months off to campaign for him.  She participated in the ___E:2008 Democratic National Convention U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Democratic_National_Convention)___ ,  where she spoke briefly about growing up with her brother and brought an Asian-American presence to the stage.

Soetoro-Ng also spoke briefly about the Obama administration's accomplishments at the ___E:2012 Democratic National Convention U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2012_Democratic_National_Convention)___ in ___E:Charlotte, North Carolina U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charlotte,_North_Carolina)___ , on September 4, 2012, sharing the podium with First Lady ___E:Michelle Obama U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michelle_Obama)___ 's older brother, former ___E:Oregon State University U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oregon_State_University)___ men's basketball team head coach, ___E:Craig Robinson U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Craig_Robinson_(basketball))___ .

In 2003,  Maya Soetoro married ___E:Konrad Ng U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Konrad_Ng)___ ( ___E:Simplified Chinese U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simplified_Chinese_characters)___ : 吴加儒), a ___E:Chinese Canadian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chinese_Canadian)___ from ___E:Burlington, Ontario U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burlington,_Ontario)___ , Canada.
Ng, who is of ___E:Malaysian Chinese U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malaysian_Chinese)___ descent, is now also a ___E:US citizen U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_citizen)___ .

He was the director of the Smithsonian Asian Pacific American Center and an assistant professor at the ___E:University of Hawaii U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Hawai%CA%BBi_at_M%C4%81noa)___ 's Academy of Creative Media.
He is now the executive director of the Doris Duke Shangri La Center for Islamic Arts and Culture in Hawaii in Honolulu, Hawaii.
They have two daughters, Suhaila  and Savita.
Soetoro-Ng has described herself as "philosophically ___E:Buddhist U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buddhist)___ ".
She speaks ___E:Indonesian U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indonesian_language)___ ,  Spanish,  and English.
